chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Signing a one-year contract with Gale Agency; Billy Shaw and Charlie Parker
summary: Cobb signs a year instead of the three Billy Shaw wanted, as Charlie Parker walks in.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So we're up there, and Billy Shaw was in California when all this was transpiring, and he came in that

morning that I went to the office that evening with Ralph. And so finally he talked me into -- well, Ralph talked me into it, and I signed a year's contract with him. I said, 'Okay, okay.' Billy come in and says to Ralph, he said, 'Oh, baby, take us a year to build him up. We need at least a three-year contract.'

I'm listening. And he turned around, and he said, 'What do you think about that, Arnett?' I said, 'I'm going to tell you what I think about it. First place, I didn't come to you all. You come to me. And I wouldn't sign three years with nobody, because I got a wife, and if we had disagreements I don't have no guarantee we're going to stay together. Might end in a divorce, and I wouldn't lay here and let you all smother me in three years. I could stand one year -- See, I'm Herbie Fields situation thinking about this (inaudible) -- and let you smother me. And we can have disagreements, and you won't do nothing for me. I plan 'Now, I can take a year because (inaudible) take six months off anyway, but I can't stand three years to be smothered under a contract. Now, you take it for what it's worth. ' Baby, this ain't fair.' I said, 'I didn't ask you to come here. Now, you remember what I said to you.' And here come Charlie Parker walking in, and Billy's talking to him. He said, 'Well, Billy, you [hooked] me thus far -- and I said I want to knock him in his head for representation of this sort. Listen to me. I'm telling you just like I felt
because I didn't want to go in it anyway.
